accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes grants under Articles 275 and 282 of the Constitution?
o: Article 275 grants are discretionary and Article 282 grants are statutory
Article 275 grants are statutory and Article 282 grants are discretionary
Both are statutory grants recommended by the Finance Commission
Both are discretionary grants released only for centrally sponsored schemes
accepted.x: Article 275 provides statutory grants-in-aid, whereas Article 282 enables discretionary grants for public purposes.
accepted.tq: Split the options by comparing the constitutional basis of the two similar provisions.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding grants under Article 275:
1. They are given to States in need of assistance as determined by Parliament.
2. They are recommended by the Finance Commission.
3. They are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Article 275 grants are statutory grants, recommended by the Finance Commission and charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
accepted.tq: Use the common constitutional features together and identify the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a normal purpose of grants under Article 275 mentioned in the Constitution’s grant framework?
o: Welfare of Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Areas
accepted.x: Article 275 grants may support revenue deficits, local bodies, disasters and tribal welfare, but financing every centrally sponsored scheme is not their general purpose.
accepted.tq: Find the option belonging to the neighbouring but distinct CSS framework.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s:
With reference to grants under Article 282, consider the following statements:
1. They may be given for any public purpose.
2. They may be given to any State.
3. They must be recommended by the Finance Commission.
4. They are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Article 282 grants may be given to any State for any public purpose. They are generally recommended or administered through Union ministries, are not required to be recommended by the Finance Commission and are not charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
accepted.tq: Test the false constitutional conditions by separating purpose, authority and chargeability.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s: Which authority generally recommends statutory grants under Article 275?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
accepted.x: Statutory grants under Article 275 are recommended by the Finance Commission.
accepted.tq: Use the authority-function association.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s: Discretionary grants under Article 282 are generally routed through which institutional channel?
accepted.x: Article 282 grants are generally administered through Union ministries; earlier, the Planning Commission was associated with this role.
accepted.tq: Identify the administrative authority rather than the constitutional recommending body.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s: Centrally Sponsored Schemes are best described as schemes which are
o: recommended only by the Finance Commission and funded only from Article 275 grants
designed by States and financed entirely by local bodies
designed by the Centre and require a matching State share
implemented without any State financial contribution
accepted.x: Centrally Sponsored Schemes are Centre-designed schemes requiring a matching contribution from the States.
accepted.tq: Apply the funding and design features to identify the scheme category.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the examples of Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
accepted.x: MGNREGA/VB-G RAM G, PMAY and NHM are examples of Centre-designed schemes. State Finance Commission grants are not a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
accepted.tq: Use the odd institutional category to eliminate the non-scheme option.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s: The allocation proposed for Centrally Sponsored Schemes in 2026–27 was
accepted.x: The CSS allocation for 2026–27 was ₹5,48,798 crore, representing a 30.6% increase according to the cited budget analysis.
accepted.tq: Compare the ascending monetary figures and identify the CSS allocation.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s: The allocation for Centrally Sponsored Schemes in 2026–27 represented an increase of
accepted.x: The CSS allocation of ₹5,48,798 crore for 2026–27 was reported as a 30.6% increase.
accepted.tq: Match the percentage specifically associated with the budget allocation.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s: Which approach was associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission’s treatment of Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
o: Linking them to measurable outcomes and reviewing inefficient schemes
Charging all CSS directly to the Consolidated Fund of India as Article 275 grants
Transferring their administration exclusively to local bodies
accepted.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission linked CSS to measurable outcomes and proposed a high-powered committee to close inefficient schemes.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy reform from its stated objective and institutional mechanism.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the grants recommended by the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: All categories of grants were discontinued
Only revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants were retained
Only local body and disaster grants were retained, while revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants were discontinued
accepted.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended only local body and disaster grants, while revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants were discontinued.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversal of retained and discontinued categories.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s: The total grants recommended by the Sixteenth Finance Commission amounted to approximately
accepted.x: The total grants recommended by the Sixteenth Finance Commission amounted to ₹9.47 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the total Finance Commission grant from local-body and earlier Commission figures.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the disaster-management grant framework associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: SDRF/SDMF corpus of ₹7,91,493 crore with 75:25 sharing for North-Eastern States
SDRF/SDMF corpus of ₹10.1 lakh crore with no State contribution
SDRF/SDMF corpus of ₹2,04,401 crore with 90:10 sharing for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and 75:25 for other States
SDRF/SDMF corpus of ₹1,55,000 crore with uniform 50:50 sharing
accepted.x: The SDRF/SDMF corpus was ₹2,04,401 crore. The cost-sharing ratio was 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and 75:25 for other States.
accepted.tq: Compare both the corpus and the differentiated cost-sharing ratios.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s: Approximately what amount of the SDRF/SDMF corpus was to be contributed by the Union?
accepted.x: The Union share in the SDRF/SDMF corpus was approximately ₹1.55 lakh crore out of the total corpus of ₹2,04,401 crore.
accepted.tq: Separate the Union contribution from the total corpus and local-body figures.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s: Which two phenomena were recommended to be notified as disasters under the disaster-grant framework?
accepted.x: Heatwave and lightning were recommended to be notified as disasters.
accepted.tq: Test the specific pair of newly proposed disaster categories.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended a total of approximately how much in grants?
accepted.x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended total grants of approximately ₹10.1 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Fifteenth Finance Commission total from the Sixteenth Finance Commission total.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s: The Fifteenth Finance Commission provided ₹4,800 crore during 2022–23 to 2025–26 for
accepted.x: An amount of ₹4,800 crore was provided to reward better educational outcomes during 2022–23 to 2025–26.
accepted.tq: Match the specific amount and period with its stated purpose.
accepted.sec: Grants-in-aid - statutory (Art. 275) vs discretionary (Art. 282), CSS

accepted.s: Under the Fourteenth Finance Commission, the total grant for local bodies was ₹2,87,436 crore. Of this, the amount allocated to panchayats was
accepted.x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission allocated ₹2,00,292 crore to panchayats out of the total local-body grant of ₹2,87,436 crore.
accepted.tq: Use the component-total relationship to identify the panchayat allocation.
accepted.sec: Local body grants - conditions, tied vs untied

accepted.s: Under the Fourteenth Finance Commission, local-body grants were distributed using which population-area formula?
accepted.x: The distribution used the 2011 population weight of 90% and area weight of 10%.
accepted.tq: Check the reversed-weight trap between population and area.
accepted.sec: Local body grants - conditions, tied vs untied

accepted.s: The approximate local-body grant recommended by the Fifteenth Finance Commission was
accepted.x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended approximately ₹4.36 lakh crore for local bodies.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the local-body total from the total grants of different Commissions.
accepted.sec: Local body grants - conditions, tied vs untied

accepted.s: The urban share in the Sixteenth Finance Commission’s local-body grants increased from 36% to
accepted.x: The urban share increased from 36% to 45%. The projected urbanisation level by 2031 was 41%, which is a separate figure.
accepted.tq: Separate the grant share from the projected urbanisation percentage.
accepted.sec: Local body grants - conditions, tied vs untied

accepted.s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission, the basic grant for local bodies consisted of
accepted.x: The basic grant constituted 80% of the local-body grant and was divided equally between tied and untied components: 50% each.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the share of the basic grant from its internal tied-untied composition.
accepted.sec: Local body grants - conditions, tied vs untied

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the performance grant under the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: It constituted 20% and was entirely untied
It constituted 50% and was equally tied and untied
It constituted 20% and was entirely tied
It constituted 80% and was entirely tied
accepted.x: The performance grant constituted 20% and was 100% untied.
accepted.tq: Match the component percentage with its tied-untied character.
accepted.sec: Local body grants - conditions, tied vs untied

accepted.s: The tied portion of the basic local-body grant was intended mainly for
o: tax administration and public debt repayment
accepted.x: The tied portion of the basic grant was earmarked for sanitation, solid-waste management and water-related purposes.
accepted.tq: Apply the expenditure-purpose linkage to identify the tied component.
accepted.sec: Local body grants - conditions, tied vs untied

accepted.s: The special infrastructure grant of ₹56,100 crore for urban local bodies was tied to
o: rural roads in villages with fewer than 10,000 people
merging all districts into urban local bodies
primary education in all metropolitan cities
wastewater management in cities having 10–40 lakh population as per 2011 data
accepted.x: The ₹56,100 crore special infrastructure grant was tied to wastewater management in cities with a 2011 population of 10–40 lakh.
accepted.tq: Combine the amount, target sector and population range to identify the grant.
accepted.sec: Local body grants - conditions, tied vs untied

accepted.s: The urbanisation premium of ₹10,000 crore was intended for
o: compensating States for GST revenue loss
merging peri-urban villages and preparing a rural-urban transition policy
accepted.x: The ₹10,000 crore urbanisation premium was a one-time grant for merging peri-urban villages and developing a rural-urban transition policy.
accepted.tq: Use the one-time nature and stated urban-transition purpose as the identifying clues.
accepted.sec: Local body grants - conditions, tied vs untied

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an entry condition for the release of local-body grants?
o: State Finance Commissions must be constituted on time
All local bodies must have identical tax rates
Local bodies must be duly constituted
accepted.x: The stated entry conditions include duly constituted local bodies, publication of audited accounts and timely constitution of State Finance Commissions. Identical tax rates are not an entry condition.
accepted.tq: Find the invented administrative condition among the genuine release conditions.
accepted.sec: Local body grants - conditions, tied vs untied

accepted.s: For release of performance grants to local bodies, which additional condition is relevant?
o: Prior approval of the Reserve Bank of India
accepted.x: Performance grants require growth in the local body’s own-source revenue, in addition to the general entry conditions.
accepted.tq: Identify the performance-related condition rather than a general institutional requirement.
accepted.sec: Local body grants - conditions, tied vs untied

accepted.s: Article 280 of the Constitution deals with the
accepted.x: Article 280 provides for the constitution of the Finance Commission by the President.
accepted.tq: Recall the constitutional article-body association.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission - Article 280, composition, functions, remit  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional status and periodicity of the Finance Commission?
o: It is a judicial body constituted by the Supreme Court whenever required
It is a statutory body constituted by the Reserve Bank every three years
It is a permanent executive body appointed annually by Parliament
It is a quasi-judicial body constituted by the President every five years or earlier
accepted.x: The Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial body constituted by the President every five years or earlier.
accepted.tq: Combine body type, appointing authority and periodicity.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission - Article 280, composition, functions, remit  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The qualifications of the members of the Finance Commission are provided under the
o: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003
accepted.x: The qualifications are prescribed under the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951.
accepted.tq: Match the statutory subject with the correct enactment and year.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission - Article 280, composition, functions, remit  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under Article 280(3)(a), the Finance Commission recommends the distribution of the net proceeds of shareable taxes
o: only between the Union and local bodies
between the Centre and States and among the States themselves
accepted.x: Article 280(3)(a) covers both vertical devolution between the Centre and States and horizontal devolution among the States.
accepted.tq: Separate vertical distribution from horizontal distribution.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission - Article 280, composition, functions, remit  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with Article 280(3)?
o: Clause (a) — maintenance of income and expenditure accounts
Clause (b) — principles governing grants-in-aid under Article 275
Clause (d) — conduct of elections to local bodies
accepted.x: Article 280(3)(b) concerns the principles governing grants-in-aid under Article 275. Clause (d) concerns any other matter referred to the Commission by the President.
accepted.tq: Use the article-clause-function pairing and reject unrelated constitutional functions.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission - Article 280, composition, functions, remit  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The provisions under Article 280(3)(bb) and 280(3)(c) relate to recommendations for augmenting the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of
o: the Reserve Bank and public sector banks
the Union Public Service Commission and Election Commission
accepted.x: These provisions concern augmenting the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of panchayats and municipalities.
accepted.tq: Identify the local-government recipients of the State Consolidated Fund augmentation.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission - Article 280, composition, functions, remit  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is a matter that may be referred to the Finance Commission by the President under Article 280(3)(d)?
o: Determination of the policy repo rate
Conduct of a census without statutory authority
Appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner
Any other matter in the interests of sound finance
accepted.x: Article 280(3)(d) permits the President to refer any other matter to the Finance Commission in the interests of sound finance.
accepted.tq: Identify the broad residual remit expressly linked with the President’s reference.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission - Article 280, composition, functions, remit  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the Finance Commission?
o: Recommending measures for augmenting State Consolidated Funds for local bodies
Recommending principles of grants-in-aid under Article 275
Recommending distribution of shareable tax proceeds
Maintaining the income and expenditure accounts of the Centre and States
accepted.x: Maintaining the income and expenditure accounts of the Centre and States is not the function of the Finance Commission. Its role is recommendatory in matters of fiscal devolution and grants.
accepted.tq: Find the administrative accounting function wrongly assigned to the Finance Commission.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission - Article 280, composition, functions, remit  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The report of the Finance Commission, together with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken, is laid before Parliament under
accepted.x: Article 281 requires the Finance Commission’s report and the memorandum explaining action taken on it to be laid before Parliament.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the article establishing the Commission from the article governing presentation of its report.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission - Article 280, composition, functions, remit  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events relating to the Sixteenth Finance Commission in chronological order:
A. Constitution of the Commission
B. Approval of the Terms of Reference
C. Commencement of the award period
D. Acceptance in the Union Budget 2026–27
accepted.x: The Terms of Reference were approved on 29 November 2023, the Commission was constituted on 31 December 2023, its recommendations were accepted in Budget 2026–27, and the award period began on 1 April 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the dates first, then place the budget acceptance before the award-period commencement.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission - Article 280, composition, functions, remit  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which additional disclosure has been recommended by the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: Annual CAG-certified disclosure of net tax proceeds
Quarterly disclosure of State election expenditure by the Election Commission
Five-yearly disclosure of local-body population by the Census Commission
Annual RBI certification of retail inflation
accepted.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended annual disclosure of net tax proceeds certified by the Comptroller and Auditor General.
accepted.tq: Match the disclosure requirement with the certifying constitutional authority.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission - Article 280, composition, functions, remit  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly represents the general net borrowing ceilings for States after 2021–22?
accepted.x: The ceiling was 3.5% in 2022–23 and 3% during 2023–24 to 2025–26.
accepted.tq: Track the year-wise downward movement rather than relying on the latest figure alone.

accepted.s: The power-sector reform-linked additional borrowing facility was available during
accepted.x: The additional 0.5% of GSDP facility was available from 2021–22 to 2024–25 and was again provided in 2025–26.
accepted.tq: Check the stated time range and the renewal year separately.

accepted.s: The approximate amount of power-sector reform-linked additional borrowing permitted in 2025–26 was
accepted.x: The additional borrowing permitted in 2025–26 under the power-sector reform linkage was approximately ₹1,71,612 crore.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the power-sector figure from the NPS/UPS contribution figure.

accepted.s: From 2022–23, States were permitted additional borrowing equal to their contributions to
accepted.x: From 2022–23, additional borrowing equal to NPS/UPS contributions was permitted; the amount was ₹62,778 crore in 2024–25.

accepted.s: The additional borrowing linked to NPS/UPS contributions amounted to how much in 2024–25?
accepted.x: The additional borrowing linked to NPS/UPS contributions was ₹62,778 crore in 2024–25.
accepted.tq: Separate the contribution-linked amount from the power-sector reform-linked amount.

accepted.s: According to the Sixteenth Finance Commission framework, the fiscal deficit of a State should be capped at
accepted.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended capping State fiscal deficits at 3% of GSDP.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the State fiscal-deficit cap from the Union’s corresponding GDP figure.
accepted.sec: State borrowing limits - net borrowing ceiling  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission framework, the Union fiscal deficit limit referred to in the material is
accepted.x: The Union fiscal deficit was specified at 3.5% of GDP, while the State cap was 3% of GSDP.
accepted.tq: Compare the Union GDP denominator with the State GSDP denominator and their respective percentages.
accepted.sec: State borrowing limits - net borrowing ceiling  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended that off-budget borrowing by States should be
o: excluded permanently from all fiscal calculations
accepted.x: The Commission recommended bringing off-budget borrowing on-budget so that the fiscal position reflects the full borrowing burden.
accepted.tq: Apply the fiscal-transparency principle to the treatment of off-budget liabilities.
